newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine economy minister says tough times ahead.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine economy minister says tough times ahead.

text.p: Viktor Suslov, after barely three weeks at the helm of troubled Ukraine's economy ministry, said on Wednesday the former Soviet republic's new government would have to take painful decisions to escape economic crisis.

"The government has a lot of preparatory work to do to bring to life a package of measures, including unpopular ones, to get the economy in order and pull it out of crisis," Suslov told a news conference.

Suslov was appointed economy minister on July 25 as part of a cabinet reshuffle which President Leonid Kuchma said was aimed at speeding up reforms. The International Monetary Fund has delayed a long-term loan pending more structural reforms and Ukraine is awaiting an interim, standby deal of about $550 million instead.
"I would like to hope that there will be a very clear shift from economic romanticism to the politics of tough economic pragmatism in the work of this government," Suslov said.
Suslov headed parliament's finance and banking committee and reactions to his appointment among analysts were mixed.
He speaks in favour of reforms but was allied with moderate conservatives in parliament, though he says he sought their backing only because they supported his committee appointment.

On Wednesday he said he favoured "sensible protectionism" including vigilance on dumping goods in Ukraine and imposing duties where appropriate on imports to the country of 51 million. He gave no specific examples.
He said he had already met Western experts including the World Bank and added: "We will put their advice to use".

Suslov confirmed that the government would press ahead with plans to cancel subsidies on communal services including rents -- a step demanded by the IMF to qualify for the multi-billion-dollar Extended Fund Facility.
A further painful step would involve making a string of big Ukrainian enterprises bankrupt.
"I have issued an order and now a list of 30 big businesses is being prepared which firstly consume a lot of energy, secondly are technically out-of-date and thirdly have big budget debts," he said.

"The aim is very simple -- to launch bankruptcy cases in the arbitrage court, stop these businesses and sell them off. There is no way out. These are steps which should have been taken a long time ago," he added.
